inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD-built, single rate for all scenarios. Cost of equity 15.5% = NZ 10y govt 4.3% + beta 1.4 x ERP 5.5% (7.7%; cyclical building-materials distributor, now levered) + 3.5% size/illiquidity premium (market cap NZ$56m, thin NZX turnover; consistent with the 2.5-3.5% used on 2CC.NZ/MOV.NZ). After-tax cost of debt 5.0% (BKBM ~3.3% + ~3.7% margin on covenant-amended facilities, x 0.72). Target weights 85/15 equity/debt (management is deleveraging; lease liabilities are charged in the flows, not in the capital structure): 0.85 x 15.5 + 0.15 x 5.0 = 13.9%, rounded to 14.0%. The user's steer toward high-teens is deliberately NOT adopted in the rate: cyclicality, the Sept-2027 refinancing, covenant risk and the exit-execution risk are charged ONCE, in the scenario flows and a 35% bear weight (owner-fcf.md s7f); stacking them into the WACC would charge them twice. The required_return_table shows the conclusion is rate-robust: the base case is negative at every rate from 9% to 17%.
notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods SKILL routing: operating company, non-US cyclical industrial -> owner-fcf.md + section 7 adaptations), component-built on a 10-year horizon so the margin can ramp from the FY2026 trough (2.3% normalised EBITDA) to a MID-CYCLE level (8.5% base) rather than extrapolating either the FY2026 loss or the FY2022 windfall. This is the user's 'mid-cycle earnings-power' routing expressed in the house engine: years 1-4 are the recovery, years 5-10 are mid-cycle, and the terminal value capitalises mid-cycle owner FCF only. An NTA/book cross-check and an orderly wind-down estimate sit in sanity_check.asset_backstop. NOT routed to the distressed-shell waterfall: the company is a going concern with facilities to Sept-2027 and positive normalised EBITDA, though the auditor's material-uncertainty paragraph is why the bear weight is 35%.

OWNER FCF (FY2026): reported FCF 5.735 (OCF 12.716 - capex 6.981) - SBC 0.657 - interest income 0.249 - lease principal 18.156 = -13.327. The IFRS-16 adjustment is the whole story: reported FCF looks positive only because NZ$18.2m of rent principal sits in financing. Lease interest 6.777 is already inside OCF.

LEASES: treatment (B) - lease cash (principal + interest, 24.9m = 5.7% of FY2026 revenue) charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (112.4m) EXCLUDED from net debt. The EBITDA margin driver is on the reported POST-IFRS16 basis (comparable to the company's normalised EBITDA) with the lease cost then deducted explicitly. D&A (1.5%) and capex (1.5%) are ex-ROU: FY2026 D&A 26.386 of which ROU depreciation 18.604 -> 7.782 non-ROU; PPE impaired to 27.2m so D&A steps down. Lease % of revenue declines from 5.4% to 4.0% (base) as two larger and seven smaller sites exit (mgmt: ~2m annualised cash saving from the seven) and revenue recovers; in dollars lease cash stays ~21-23m, i.e. never below the FY2023 level plus Perry's sites.

MID-CYCLE ANCHOR: post-IFRS16 normalised EBITDA margins FY2021-26 were 8.0 / 11.1 / 9.0 / 7.5 / 0.5 / 2.3% (avg 6.4%; ex the FY2022 steel-price windfall 5.5%). EBITDA after full lease cost: 4.3 / 8.1 / 5.7 / 3.2 / -5.1 / -3.4%. Base assumes the reset business (reinforcing/wire and plate exited, removing ~7.5m of normalised EBIT losses; ~6m phase-3 cost-out of which 3.5m landed in FY26; site exits ~2m) reaches 8.5% post-IFRS16 by FY2031 - FY2024's 7.5% plus roughly half the reset benefit - on volumes near FY2024's 115kt for the continuing product set. Bull reaches FY2022/23-like 10.5%; bear stalls at 6.0%, below FY2024, on import competition and a recovery that keeps slipping.

WORKING CAPITAL: distributor NWC (inventory 111.0 + receivables 65.7 - payables 66.2) is ~25% of revenue, so growth CONSUMES cash: wc_capture_pct = -25 (bull -20 on SKU rationalisation). FY2027's revenue decline (exits) therefore releases cash, which stands in for management's guided NZ$11-12m of exit proceeds (inventory + plant) - not separately added, to avoid double-counting. Note FY2026 payables jumped 18.6m (creditor stretch) - a reversal risk not modelled.

TAX: NZ 28% statutory. Cash tax is ZERO through FY2031 in base: ~64m of tax losses (FY2025-26 pre-tax losses ex impairment) plus 14.5m of DTA on the impairment timing differences; DTA 30.0m at 30-Jun-2026. Ramped 10/20/28% over FY2032-34 so the shelter is NOT perpetuated into the terminal. Bear: never pays tax (never profitable). A rescue raise that breaches the 49% shareholder-continuity test would forfeit the losses - a bear-case detail.

REVENUE: FY2027 -5% base is the net of ~12-13% of revenue leaving with reinforcing/wire and plate (Processing segment 165.1m; reinforcing/wire/plate estimated ~55m) and ~+7% underlying recovery (FY2026 volumes +15.9%, H2 FY26 ~40% ahead of H1). Growth then 6/5/4/3% decaying to 2% (NZ nominal construction-volume recovery), so revenue only regains FY2016's 516m in FY2033 - the through-cycle revenue CAGR is negative and is not extrapolated.
SBC: 0.657m (0.15% of revenue) expensed and held at 0.15%; house/street band is ~NZ$0.02 wide, so band_position is reported as null (degenerate), not 0.

NOT IN THE MODEL: impairment reversals (non-cash); the 1.7m loan receivable; the anti-dilutive options; any takeover premium (see asset_backstop.trade_sale_reference); the Commerce Commission outcome on the Euro Corporation sale (a delayed or blocked sale is the bear).

ELECTION/MACRO: NZ general election 7-Nov-2026 and the H2-FY27 recovery management's own covenant forecast depends on are the two dated events that move FY2027 drivers; refresh after the Feb-2027 H1 result.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: NZ nominal construction-volume/GDP proxy for the terminal path. Every historical CAGR is negative (revenue -1.6%/10y, equity -3.8%/10y) or undefined (EPS and owner FCF negative at the FY2026 endpoint); none is usable as a forward driver.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-16.4% 3y) diverges from revenue CAGR (-9.4% 3y) by more than 30%: equity is being destroyed faster than revenue is shrinking (two impairment cycles, FY2018/20 and FY2026). EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined because both endpoints are negative.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income - IFRS-16 lease principal) averaged NZ$5.0m/yr over FY2016-26 and NZ$3.8m/yr over the FY2021-26 cycle, against a NZ$56m market cap and NZ$48m of net bank debt. FY2022 (-53.6) and FY2023 (+76.9) are one working-capital sawtooth and net to +23.3 over two years; never use either alone. Reported FCF overstates owner FCF by NZ$13-18m a year since IFRS-16 (FY2020).

scenario_narratives.bear: Recovery slips again. The 7-Nov-2026 election and a still-weak commercial construction pipeline keep H1 FY27 loss-making; the Euro Corporation sale is delayed or blocked by the Commerce Commission so reinforcing/wire winds down at cost rather than being sold; import competition keeps product margin/tonne flat. Revenue -8% in FY2027 and only 1-3% after; post-IFRS16 EBITDA stalls at 6.0% (below FY2024) while lease cash stays 4.6-4.8% of a smaller revenue base, so EBIT after rent never turns positive and owner FCF is negative every year. Net debt drifts toward the NZ$80m facility ceiling, the quarterly earnings covenant is breached in FY27 (Event of Review under the amended terms), and the September-2027 refinancing is achieved only with a deeply discounted rescue placement (bear_case_detail). Terminal value hits the zero floor: on these flows the business cannot service NZ$21m of rent plus NZ$48m of debt, and the equity is worth nothing on cash flows.
scenario_narratives.base: Gradual, uneven recovery on management's own H2-FY27 timing. Reinforcing/wire and plate exit during FY2027 (revenue -5% net of ~7% underlying growth), removing ~7.5m of normalised EBIT losses; the remaining ~2.5m of phase-3 cost-out and ~2m of site-exit savings land in FY2028. Post-IFRS16 EBITDA margin ramps 4.5 -> 8.5% by FY2031 (FY2024's 7.5% plus half the reset benefit), on revenue that only regains FY2016 levels in FY2033. Lease cash falls to 4.0% of revenue but stays ~NZ$21m. Cash tax is nil to FY2031 on tax losses then ramps to 28%. Mid-cycle owner FCF is NZ$8-10m a year - the FY2021/FY2024 experience - and after NZ$48m of net debt that is worth roughly nothing to equity at 14%. The covenant forecast holds, no raise is needed, and the equity survives as an option on the bull case or a trade sale.
scenario_narratives.bull: The cycle turns on time and the reset works. Government infrastructure and social-housing spend lands in H2 CY2026, residential consents follow the OCR cuts, and continuing volumes recover toward 140kt by FY2030 with product margin/tonne holding above NZ$1,200 as low-margin rebar leaves the mix. Perry galvanizing grows ahead of business case. Revenue +9/8/6% in FY2028-30; post-IFRS16 EBITDA reaches FY2022/23-like 10.5% by FY2031; lease cash falls to 3.4% of revenue after the nine site exits; working-capital intensity improves to 20% on SKU rationalisation. Owner FCF reaches ~NZ$19m and the terminal is Gordon at 2% (12x cap not binding). Even so the bull case is worth about NZ$0.20-0.25 - a peak-margin business held for a decade barely covers today's price, which is why this scenario carries only 20%.

bear.fcf_basis: unlevered owner FCF, treatment B: lease principal AND interest charged inside the flows (lease_cost), IFRS-16 lease liabilities excluded from net debt; SBC expensed; interest income excluded

base.fcf_basis: unlevered owner FCF, treatment B: lease principal AND interest charged inside the flows (lease_cost), IFRS-16 lease liabilities excluded from net debt; SBC expensed; interest income excluded

bull.fcf_basis: unlevered owner FCF, treatment B: lease principal AND interest charged inside the flows (lease_cost), IFRS-16 lease liabilities excluded from net debt; SBC expensed; interest income excluded

entry_price.method: price at which buying today, collecting the projected owner FCF and exiting in FY2036 earns a 15% IRR; terminal value REBUILT at the hurdle rate: min(Gordon@15%, cap x FCF_10), floored at zero; net debt deducted; divided by the flat diluted count (repo standard 2026-09-01).
entry_price.reading: There is no price at which the weighted case returns 15%: the bear and base entry prices are negative (the flows do not cover net debt). Only the bull case has a positive hurdle price, and it is well below NZ$0.305. A buyer today is underwriting the bull case or a trade sale, not a 15% cash-flow return.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's required return (min(Gordon@r, cap x FCF_10), floored at zero). The 15% row equals the base entry price and the 14% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value. The base case is negative at EVERY rate: the verdict does not depend on the WACC.

sensitivity.note: Base scenario, NZ$ per share; WACC +/-2pp around 14%, terminal growth +/-1pp around 1.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 35% (house default 15%): the FY2026 audit report carries a material-uncertainty-related-to-going-concern paragraph; covenants were re-cut mid-year and breach consequences moved to 'Event of Review'; the NZ$50m RCF/term facilities expire 4-Sep-2027 and the NZ$20m trade loan is repayable on demand; management's own covenant forecast 'assumes a market recovery in the second half of FY27' that has now been pushed out three years running. Base 45%: management's timing, half the reset benefit. Bull 20% (house 35%): needs three independent things - macro recovery on time, clean exits including Commerce Commission clearance, and a margin re-rating to FY2022/23 levels - and even then is worth little more than today's price.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC is 0.15% of revenue: house and street values differ by ~NZ$0.02/share and the price sits far outside the band (above both). Reported as null rather than a degenerate percentage.
probability_weighted.limited_liability_note: Negative per-share values measure how far the flows fall short of covering net debt; a shareholder's loss is capped at the price paid. The floored memo (bear at 0) is the expected value to a holder who walks away in the bear case; it is still below the current price.

bear_case_detail.covenant_and_refinancing: Facilities NZ$80m committed (20m RCA + 30m term to 4-Sep-2027; 30m trade loan on demand), 60m drawn at 30-Jun-2026. Covenants: quarterly earnings and net debt targets, amended during FY26, breach -> Event of Review. Directors' forecast compliance is 'highly dependent on assumptions regarding improved trading performance'. Auditor: material uncertainty related to going concern.

rescue_raise_memo.assumption: NZ$40m placement/rights at NZ$0.15 (a ~50% discount to the current price, in line with distressed NZX recaps) = 266.7m new shares -> 450.3m on issue; proceeds repay bank debt so net debt falls to ~8m; the business then follows the BASE path.
rescue_raise_memo.reading: A recap does not create value, it transfers it: existing holders keep ~40% of a business whose base-case EV is ~NZ$25m. Their residual is a few cents. Tax-loss forfeiture under the 49% continuity test would make it worse.

sanity_check.basis: Owner-FCF basis in the model (SBC expensed, lease cash in flows, leases out of net debt). Historical table: user-supplied June FY-end closes; market cap on the period's share count (FY2017-18 on 90.6m pre-raise shares); EV ex-lease = market cap + bank debt - cash; the lease-inclusive column adds IFRS-16 lease liabilities (FY2020+ only). EBITDA is normalised where the company published it (FY2021-26), statutory before that; FY2016-19 EBITDA is pre-IFRS16 (rent in opex) so EV/EBITDA is not comparable across the FY2020 break.
sanity_check.share_basis_break: FY2019 rights issue/placement took shares from 90.6m to 166.0m; FY2025 Perry scrip took them to 183.6m. FY2017-18 per-share multiples are on the old base and are NOT comparable per share, only at the market-cap level (P/B, P/Sales, EV/EBITDA are unaffected; P/E is affected via EPS).
outlier_years_excluded: FY2026 (impairment years: statutory EBITDA/earnings negative; P/E and EV/EBITDA undefined)

implied_multiples.note: Base IV is negative, so every implied multiple is negative/degenerate: the DCF sits BELOW every multiple the market has ever paid. Trip logic (implied > 2x historical average) cannot fire; the relevant test is the opposite one - whether the asset backstop should override the earnings value - handled in asset_backstop.

price_range_10y.note: Price is AT the 10-year low (and the 52-week low). The SEK.NZ trap (high upside at the top of the range) does not apply; the risk here is the opposite one - a value trap where the asset value never converts to cash.

sanity_check.pe_test: NOT MEANINGFUL: FY2026 EPS -33.3c and base-case earnings are near zero through FY2029; historical P/E (7-14x in profitable years) is quoted for the record only.

exit_multiple_cap_8c_5_4.cap: terminal value capped at 10x owner FCF (base; 8x bear, 12x bull) AND checked against the 10-year P/B ceiling of 1.0x and the FY2021-24 EV/EBITDA range (ex-lease EV on post-IFRS16 EBITDA: min/avg/max below)

exit_multiple_cap_ev_ebitda.basis: ex-lease EV / normalised post-IFRS16 EBITDA, FY2021-24 (10yr min / avg / max per Step 8c.5.4); lease-inclusive equivalents [5.3, 6.15, 7.1]

exit_multiple_cap_8c_5_4.note: Neither cap binds in any scenario: the model terminal values (0 / 70 / 189) sit far below the EV/EBITDA-capped values (see exit_multiple_cap_tv_by_scenario); the base Gordon TV at 14%/1.5% is ~1.5x terminal EBITDA (ex-lease) and ~0.1x projected book, below anything the market has paid. The cap exists to stop a re-rating being smuggled into the terminal; here the terminal is already below every historical anchor.

sanity_check.diagnosis: No over-valuation trip: the base IV is below zero, i.e. below every multiple the market has paid in ten years (P/B 0.51-1.00x, P/Sales 0.14-0.41x). The check therefore runs in reverse - is the DCF too harsh relative to the asset base? The asset_backstop block answers that: NTA NZ$0.40 is real on the balance sheet but converts to cash only through a trade sale (~NZ$0.22-0.34/share at 0.20-0.25x sales); in a wind-down the leases and bank debt absorb it. The price of NZ$0.305 is consistent with the market paying for that option, and the DCF is consistent with the cash flows not supporting it.

asset_backstop.nta_composition_fy2026: equity 121.759 less intangibles 47.655 (incl. galvanizing goodwill 23.3) = 74.104; DTA of 30.003 is INSIDE NTA and only worth anything if the company earns taxable profit

mid_cycle_ev_ebitda_cross_check.why_not_headline: The multiple the market paid for STU over FY2017-FY2024 was, ex post, wrong: the price fell 87% while book value fell 43%. Historical multiples here are evidence of serial over-valuation, not of fair value. The same mid-cycle EBITDA discounted at 14% after the NZ$21m/yr of rent, D&A/capex and working capital that the multiple ignores is worth roughly nothing to equity.

orderly_wind_down_estimate.reading: NTA is not realisable in a wind-down: the 112m lease book and 60m of bank debt rank ahead, and inventory/PPE realise well below book. The NZ$0.40 NTA is only reachable through a trade buyer who wants the network as a going concern.

trade_sale_reference.note: A Vulcan/Fletcher-type acquirer paying 0.20-0.25x sales for the distribution network (STU's own 10-year P/Sales range is 0.14-0.41x) would deliver ~NZ$0.22-0.34 per share - roughly the current price. This is the option the market is paying for; it is not in the three cash-flow scenarios because there is no live approach.

asset_backstop.conclusion: Earnings value (weighted IV) is below zero; asset value is NZ$0.40 (NTA) / NZ$0.66 (book) but not realisable except via a trade sale worth roughly the current price. The market price of NZ$0.305 sits between the cash-flow value and the asset value: it is paying ~0.46x book / 0.76x NTA for a takeover-or-recovery option, not for the cash flows.

valuation_philosophy: This is a mid-cycle earnings-power valuation with an asset cross-check, not a growth DCF. Steel & Tube is a price-taking steel distributor in one small economy: eleven years of results sum to a net loss, revenue is lower than in FY2016, two impairment cycles have destroyed NZ$110m of equity, and the dividend is suspended. So the model does not extrapolate the FY2026 loss (a trough with a NZ$51.9m non-cash impairment) or the FY2022 windfall (a steel-price inventory gain that reversed the next year); it ramps margins over four years to a mid-cycle level - roughly FY2024 plus half the benefit of exiting reinforcing/wire and plate - and capitalises only that. The adjustment that decides the answer is IFRS-16: reported free cash flow looks positive because NZ$18m of rent principal sits in financing. Charge the full NZ$25m of lease cash, and mid-cycle owner FCF is NZ$8-10m a year against NZ$48m of net bank debt. At a 14% cost of capital that leaves the equity worth roughly nothing in the base case, negative in the bear (the flows cannot service rent plus debt and a rescue raise would dilute existing holders to a few cents), and about NZ$0.20-0.25 in a bull case that assumes FY2022/23-level margins for a decade. The asset side says something different: NTA is NZ$0.40 a share and book value NZ$0.66, and the market has paid 0.5-1.0x book for ten years. But that book has never been converted into shareholder cash - the price fell 87% while the market paid those multiples - and in a wind-down the leases and bank debt absorb it. NTA is reachable only through a trade buyer who wants the network, and a 0.20-0.25x-sales bid is worth roughly today's price. So NZ$0.305 is not irrational: it is the market paying about 0.46x book for a takeover-or-recovery option. What the model says is that the cash flows do not support it, there is no price at which a 15% return is available on the weighted case, and a holder is underwriting either the bull case or a bid. Not a buy on this analysis; the honest label is 'speculative option, no margin of safety'.
